title: People Ops — Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Maya Chen
summary: Company-wide people operations guide covering standardized hiring workflows, manager responsibilities for onboarding, and the performance & feedback cycle. Intended as the source of truth for managers and people-ops partners.
body:
Overview

This document describes Redwood Inference’s standardized hiring process, the recommended employee onboarding flow, and the performance & feedback cycle with practical manager guidance. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and engineering managers who run teams with LLM inference product responsibilities.

Contents
- Hiring process and SLAs
- Interview loop, scorecards, and interviewer guidance
- Offer approval, compensation, and background checks
- Pre-day-zero and first-90-days onboarding checklists
- Manager responsibilities and 1:1 cadence
- Performance review cycle, calibration, and promotion guidance
- Templates and examples (job posting, scorecard, onboarding checklist)

1) Hiring process and SLAs

Goal: hire high-quality engineers and product candidates with predictable timelines and an inclusive, consistent candidate experience.

Key metrics and targets
- Time-to-offer (target): 35 calendar days from requisition approval to signed offer
- Pipeline conversion: aim for 15–25% of onsite interviews leading to hire
- Interview completion SLA: schedule technical interviews within 7 business days of candidate screening
- Offer acceptance rate target: >= 70% for top-of-funnel candidates

Standard workflow (high level)
1. Requisition creation and approval (Hiring manager + People Ops) — include role brief and competency rubric.
2. Sourcing and screening (Recruiter) — initial screen + resume review within 3 business days.
3. Technical bar check / take-home (optional) — use only when role requires measurable takeaways. Keep take-homes <= 4 hours.
4. Interview loop (onsite / virtual) — 3–5 interviews: system design/problem solving, product/behavioral, and role-specific deep dive.
5. Debrief and decision (Hiring manager + interviewers + recruiter) — use structured scorecards.
6. Compensation approval and offer (People Ops + Hiring manager) — include target total compensation and equity guidelines.
7. Background check and reference checks (People Ops)
8. Onboarding and first-90-day plan (Hiring manager + People Ops)

Requisition checklist (required at creation)
- Role summary and responsibilities
- Target level and ladder alignment (link to leveling doc)
- Hiring committee members and interview packet owners
- Diversity sourcing plan and inclusive language check

2) Interview loop, scorecards, and interviewer guidance

Interview structure (recommended for engineering roles)
- 30–45 min initial screen (recruiter or hiring manager) — culture fit, motivation, logistics
- 60 min technical coding/problem solving — focus on fundamentals, clarifying assumptions, and communication
- 60 min system design or architecture deep dive — align to Redwood’s runtime and platform priorities where relevant
- 45–60 min behavioral/product interview — collaboration, ownership, cross-team communication
- Optional manager interview and compensation conversation

Scorecard fields (use structured ratings: 1–5 and pass/fail criteria)
- Technical skills (algorithms, systems, product-specific knowledge)
- Problem-solving approach (clarity, tradeoffs, testing)
- Communication (explainability, listening, feedback receptivity)
- Collaboration & cultural add (ownership, cross-functional influence)
- Role-specific requirements (e.g., GPU/infra experience, cloud ops, model-serving knowledge)
- Overall recommendation (strong hire / hire / neutral / no hire)

Interviewer expectations
- Complete scorecards within 24 hours of interview
- Provide specific examples and rationale for each rating
- Surface any concerns early (compensation expectations, notice period)
- Avoid asking about protected characteristics; focus on job-relevant competencies

Debrief best practices
- Hiring manager facilitates; keep to 30–45 minutes
- Use scorecard averages but prioritize qualitative evidence for hire/no-hire decisions
- Document blocking concerns in the debrief notes

3) Offer approval, compensation, and background checks

Compensation approval steps
1. Hiring manager proposes base, bonus, and equity per leveling guidelines
2. People Ops validates against band, internal comp equity, and market benchmarks
3. Final approval from HR lead for offers > 10% outside band or senior IC/manager hires

Offer components
- Base salary, target bonus structure, equity grant range, and benefits summary
- Expected start date, remote/office expectations, and relocation (if applicable)
- Contingency clauses: background check and employment verification

Background & references
- People Ops conducts reference checks for finalists prior to offer extension where required by role
- Standard background checks initiated after signed offer and acceptance per vendor SLA (typically 3–10 business days)

4) Onboarding: pre-day-zero, first day, week 1, and first 90 days

Principles: reduce cognitive load, create early wins, and connect new hire to team, product, and company mission. Managers are accountable for the 90-day success plan; People Ops provides operational support.

Pre-day-zero (people-ops + manager)
- Confirm equipment order, access to Slack/GSuite/GitHub, and required accounts
- Share welcome packet (culture, org chart, first-week agenda)
- Schedule 1:1 on day 1 and weekly 1:1s for first 90 days

First day
- Team welcome and introductions (brief 30–45 minutes)
- HR orientation (benefits, payroll, security training)
- Access verification and dev workstation setup (IT + Eng infra)

Week 1 (focus: context and small wins)
- Pairing sessions with buddy (assigned by manager)
- First contribution: an onboarding ticket scoped to finish within 3–5 days
- Product and system walkthroughs: runtime architecture, services, and onboarding docs

30/60/90 day milestones (manager-owned)
- 30 days: understands codebase, can complete small PRs independently, active in team rituals
- 60 days: delivering features with minimal oversight, owns at least one small cross-functional task
- 90 days: operating at expected level for the role; manager and peer feedback collected and documented

Onboarding checklist (template snippet)
- Accounts provisioned: Slack, Google, Jira, GitHub, CI dashboard
- Hardware delivered and verified
- Security training completed: data handling, SSO, MFA, code-of-conduct
- First-PR checklist and reviewer assigned

5) Manager responsibilities and cadence

Primary manager responsibilities
- Run inclusive hiring and ensure interviewers complete scorecards
- Create and own a 90-day success plan with measurable outcomes
- Hold weekly 1:1s and weekly syncs during first 30 days; move to bi-weekly regular cadence thereafter
- Provide timely feedback (praise and corrective) and document conversations in performance system
- Advocate for direct reports during calibration and promotion discussions

1:1 guidance
- Cadence: weekly for new reports, then at least every 2 weeks
- Typical 1:1 agenda: status updates, roadblocks, career conversation, feedback exchange, well-being check
- Use structured notes and follow-up actions; share relevant learning resources and goal checkpoints

Manager hiring checklist (short)
- Create role brief and rubric
- Build interview packet and identify interviewers
- Partner with recruiter on sourcing and diversity plan

6) Performance and feedback cycle

Cadence & timeline (annual cycle example)
- Quarterly goals (OKRs/team milestones) set at team level and aligned to product roadmap
- Mid-year check-in (informal): manager + peer feedback and career development conversation
- Annual performance review: written self-assessment, manager assessment, calibration, and calibration meeting
- Promotion windows: semi-annual (Q2 and Q4) with supporting evidence and calibration notes

Review components
- Goal achievement (quantitative milestones)
- Role competency (ladder expectations)
- Impact & leadership (scope, influence, execution quality)
- Peer and stakeholder feedback

Calibration & promotion guidance
- Managers submit dossiers with evidence (PRs, project outcomes, customer/partner feedback)
- Calibration panel includes HR, hiring managers, and an independent engineering leader for impartiality
- Promotion decisions require documented examples that map to ladder criteria and at least two independent supporting reviewers

Corrective performance process
- If performance concerns arise: manager documents expectations, creates a performance improvement plan (PIP) with clear metrics and check-ins (30–90 day duration), and engages People Ops early for consistency and legal compliance

7) Career development and learning

- Managers should run quarterly career check-ins and identify training, mentorship, or rotational opportunities.
- People Ops maintains a learning stipend policy (see People Ops learning-stipend page) and recommended technical learning paths for platform, infra, and applied ML.

8) Offboarding (brief)

- Initiated by People Ops when resignation or termination is confirmed
- Manager completes knowledge transfer, final deliverables, and access removal checklist with IT and Security
- Exit interview scheduled with People Ops to capture feedback

9) Templates and examples (copyable snippets)

Job posting snippet (example)
```
Title: Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Summary: Build and scale Redwood’s GPU-optimized inference runtime. Work on kernel selection, batching, and latency-critical systems with cross-functional product partners.
Responsibilities:
- Design and implement high-throughput inference features
- Ship reliable, observable services with strong testing and instrumentation
- Collaborate with research and infra teams on model-serving optimizations
Requirements:
- 5+ years systems engineering experience, distributed systems background
- Experience with GPU-accelerated workloads or model-serving stacks
Preferred:
- Familiarity with quantization, KV cache management, or custom kernel optimizations
```

Interview scorecard (example fields)
- Candidate name | Role | Interviewer | Date
- Technical skills (1-5): evidence and notes
- System design (1-5): evidence and notes
- Communication & collaboration (1-5): evidence and notes
- Overall (strong hire / hire / neutral / no hire): rationale

Onboarding ticket example (GitHub issue description)
- Title: Onboard: Fix linting in auth-service to enable local dev
- Description: Short task that touches the codebase and CI; reviewer: assigned buddy
- Success criteria: PR merged, CI green, reviewer feedback incorporated

10) Ownership, escalation, and support

Who to contact
- Recruiter or People Ops partner: for role approvals, offer questions, and background checks
- IT/Eng Infra: hardware provisioning and access issues
- Security: required compliance training or sensitive access requests

Escalation matrix (examples)
- Offer delays > 10 business days: escalate to People Ops lead (people-ops-lead@redwood.ai)
- New hire access not provisioned by day 2: escalate to IT ops

Related resources
- Link: Leveling and compensation guidelines (internal)
- Link: Engineering onboarding playbook (eng-developer-experience)
- Link: Diversity hiring checklist (people-ops/diversity)

Appendix: common QA and guidance
- Can we use take-homes? Yes, but keep them short and role-relevant. Always provide extension windows for candidates with constraints.
- What about remote hires and relocation? People Ops will provide relocation guidelines and remote onboarding checklist per location.
- Who approves exceptions to comp bands? HR lead + Finance approval for exceptions > 10% outside band.

Document maintenance
- Owner: People Ops (Maya Chen).
- Review cadence: annual or upon major policy change.
- Change log: 2025-09-15 created; 2026-02-10 updated with promotion cadence and onboarding checklist clarifications.
